ranking_quote: 4,C0029,Spielman-Teng conjecture on the least singular value of Bernoulli matrices,attempted_un,Spielman-Teng constant one
exact_statement: For B_n with mutually independent uniform {-1,+1} entries, find c in (0,1) such that P(s_min(B_n) <= epsilon/sqrt(n)) <= epsilon + c^n for every epsilon >= 0 (asymptotically in n).
original_primary_source: Spielman and Teng, Smoothed Analysis of Algorithms, ICM 2002, Conjecture 2, printed p.605 (arXiv:math/0212413v1, PDF p.9): https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0212413
original_primary_scope: For a d-by-d matrix of independent uniform signs, P(||A^{-1}||>T) <= sqrt(d)/T + alpha^n for an absolute alpha<1 (the paper prints n in the exponent although it calls the dimension d). The singular event is included by the T=infinity remark. The modern smallest-singular-value formulation uses continuity from above to handle <= thresholds.
statement_source: Sah, Sahasrabudhe, Sawhney, On the Spielman-Teng Conjecture, arXiv:2405.20308v2 (2025), Introduction equations (1)-(2): https://arxiv.org/html/2405.20308
statement_source_quote: they conjectured that ... P(sigma_n(B) <= epsilon n^{-1/2}) <= epsilon + e^{-Omega(n)}, for all epsilon >= 0
earlier_source: Bordenave and Chafai, Around the circular law, arXiv:1109.3343v4, p.53: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1109.3343
earlier_source_quote: there exists a constant 0 < c < 1 such that P(sqrt(n) s_n(X) <= t) <= t + c^n for n >> 1 and any small enough t >= 0
strongest_verified_prior_theorem: Sah-Sahasrabudhe-Sawhney Theorem 1.1: for iid mean-zero variance-one subgaussian entries and all epsilon>=0, upper bound (1+o(1))epsilon+e^{-Omega_xi(n)}, with o(1) decaying as C_xi(log n)^(-1/16). Theorem 1.2 compares to the finite-n Gaussian probability with the same relative error and an exponential additive term.
